problem_statement: The end-of-run deploy job crashes whenever the change policy service times out on a single request. `run_deploy_queue` lets `PolicyTimeout` escape from the event bus, so the CI job fails and every deploy queued after the slow request is left unprocessed. Runs should finish cleanly when the policy service is slow: the remaining requests must still be processed and each request should end up with an outcome in the returned results. `tests/test_pipeline.py::test_policy_timeout_does_not_abort_queue` reproduces it.

issue_paraphrases: The end-of-run deploy job crashes whenever the change policy service times out on a single request. `run_deploy_queue` lets `PolicyTimeout` escape from the event bus, so the CI job fails and every deploy queued after the slow request is left unprocessed. Runs should finish cleanly when the policy service is slow: the remaining requests must still be processed and each request should end up with an outcome in the returned results. `tests/test_pipeline.py::test_policy_timeout_does_not_abort_queue` reproduces it.

When the change policy service times out on even one request, the end-of-run deploy job crashes. `PolicyTimeout` escapes from the event bus inside `run_deploy_queue`, which makes the CI job fail and leaves every deploy queued after the slow request unprocessed. A slow policy service should not stop runs from finishing cleanly: the remaining requests still need to be processed, and every request should have an outcome in the returned results. Reproduced by `tests/test_pipeline.py::test_policy_timeout_does_not_abort_queue`.

A single request timing out against the change policy service is enough to crash the end-of-run deploy job. Because `run_deploy_queue` allows `PolicyTimeout` to escape from the event bus, the CI job fails and none of the deploys queued behind the slow request get processed. Expected behavior: runs finish cleanly even if the policy service is slow, the remaining requests are still processed, and each request ends up with an outcome in the returned results. See `tests/test_pipeline.py::test_policy_timeout_does_not_abort_queue` for a reproduction.

Problem: the end-of-run deploy job crashes any time the change policy service times out on one request. `run_deploy_queue` does not stop `PolicyTimeout` from escaping the event bus, so the CI job fails and all deploys queued after the slow request remain unprocessed. Desired outcome: when the policy service is slow, runs should still finish cleanly, with the remaining requests processed and an outcome recorded for each request in the returned results. The test `tests/test_pipeline.py::test_policy_timeout_does_not_abort_queue` reproduces this.
